implementation_issues.description: The paper names four published implied-cost estimators and averages them, but does not reproduce estimator-level formulas, terminal assumptions or model-specific forecast/book-equity settings; exact COC construction cannot be verified from this article alone.

review_notes: Selected the one frozen full-period Table 4 Panel A baseline, 1995–2006, N=6,456. The N=2,846 transition-excluded column is sensitivity analysis; Panels B/C reconstruct comparisons from Panel A.

The sample contains 1,084 firms from 18 EU countries and requires both pre- and post-adoption years. Aggregate counts and bounded probes do not confirm exact local cohort coverage; no coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied.

Fiscal-year labels are not actual FYE dates. Price/forecast inputs occur seven months after FYE and may reach calendar 2007 for FY2006. INFLA is next-year monthly inflation; exact fiscal/calendar join is unresolved.
Datastream and World Bank are both named for INFLA. The official current World Bank database is only a later-vintage candidate and does not substitute for Datastream.
No author-prepared dataset was used as a primary route; no local coverage or access-blocked status was inferred.

evidence.quote: I use a measure that relies on four estimation models: the industry ROE model in Gebhardt et al. (2001), the economywide growth model in Claus and Thomas (2001), the unrestricted abnormal earnings growth model in Gode and Mohanram (2003), and the restricted abnormal earnings growth model in Easton (2004).
evidence.description: COC averages four named implied-cost estimators; full formulas/settings are not reproduced in this article.

evidence.quote: A firm is classified as a mandatory adopter if the data item ‘‘astd’’ (accounting standards) in Compustat Global does not equal ‘‘DI’’ prior to 2005.
evidence.description: Primary adopter coding uses item astd and DI before 2005.

evidence.quote: three forms of U.S. cross-listing (from JP Morgan ADR Analytics)
evidence.description: The PP, OTC and EXCH controls are sourced to JP Morgan ADR Analytics.

evidence.quote: the expected future inflation rate estimated by the median of next year’s monthly inflation rates (from Datastream and the World Bank; INFLA)
evidence.description: INFLA uses next-year country-specific monthly inflation jointly attributed to Datastream and World Bank.

evidence.quote: firm size (SIZE), measured as the natural logarithm of total assets in U.S. dollars at year-end, return variability (RETVAR), computed as the annual standard deviation of monthly stock returns at year-end, and financial leverage (LEV), estimated as the ratio of total liabilities over total assets at year-end
evidence.description: Year-end control definitions and annual monthly-return window.

evidence.quote: I winsorize all firm-level continuous variables at the top and bottom 1 percent of their distributions, with the exception of firm size (log of total assets).
